concept: The story is a role reversal: the champion is the outsider. So the hero runs the usual Krayon setup in grey (Gukesh is the world champion) and flips it in white (he starts as the underdog), with the two world rankings, No.4 and No.26, as the facts underneath. Slide 2 is the evidence as a rating bar chart that only counts points above 2700, so the 72-point gap reads as a long glowing bar against a stub. Then two giant numbers (2-0 head to head and Sindarov's unbeaten 10/14), the money at stake, and a closing slide that argues the other side before handing fans the pick. Indian orange, type and shapes only: no player photos, no FIDE or event logos.
caption:
Gukesh is the world champion. In Geneva he starts as the underdog.

Game 1 against Javokhir Sindarov is tomorrow at 7:30 pm IST. Sindarov is world No. 4 on 2782. Gukesh is No. 26 on 2710. The Uzbek leads their classical head to head 2-0 with one draw and won the Candidates unbeaten on 10/14.

But matches are not ratings. Gukesh beat Ding Liren 7.5-6.5 for the title in 2024 and beat Sindarov in rapid this year. Both are 20, the youngest title match ever. 14 games, first to 7.5 points and $200,000 for every game won.

Who wins: Gukesh or Sindarov? Tell us below.

Figures via ChessBase India, Chess.com and FIDE's WorldChess.
